title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse of deployed data systems rather than a failure of the systems' own outputs. A former sheriff's deputy is alleged to have used the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and GCIC database for personal reasons, including tracking a woman without her consent. The tools were doing what they were built to do, and the person using them held credentials that authorised the access.

The failure sits at the query and access layer, not in the cameras or the database. Access was granted by role, so each lookup would have looked legitimate in isolation, and the misuse only becomes visible when individual queries are tied to a stated purpose. Catching it would have required logging and review of who searched for whom, and a check that connected each search to an actual case.

The indictment of eight counts is an allegation, and no verdict has been reached. The reporting does not establish intent beyond what prosecutors charge, and the outcome of the arraignment is not yet known.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been indicted on eight counts after a Georgia Bureau of Investigation inquiry. The charges include four counts of violating his oath as a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege he misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and GCIC database for personal and unlawful reasons, including tracking and surveilling a woman without consent between April 10 and May 1, 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman, who spoke anonymously, said she hopes her story helps other women report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court. The GBI led the investigation after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested an independent review in 2024.
